On the Effective Date, all recipients of New Common Stock shall be deemed to have accepted and shall be bound by the Shareholders\' Agreement, substantially in the form included as Plan Supplement Exhibit C. The Shareholders\' Agreement shall include, without limitation: (i) customary registration rights, including demand and piggyback registration rights; (ii) transfer restrictions restricting the sale, transfer, or other disposition of New Common Stock for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Effective Date; and (iii) tag-along and drag-along rights on customary terms.

The Plan contemplates the adoption of a Management Incentive Plan reserving up to eight percent (8%) of the fully diluted reorganized equity of Reorganized Oakvale for issuance to management participants. The final terms of the MIP, including the form of equity awards (which may consist of stock options, restricted stock units, or other equity-based awards), vesting schedules, exercise prices, and allocation among individual participants, shall be determined by agreement between the Required Consenting First Lien Lenders and Gerald T. Harwick, the Chief Executive Officer. The MIP term sheet shall be finalized as promptly as practicable following the Effective Date. On the Effective Date, all existing equity securities, notes, bonds, indentures, certificates, instruments, and agreements evidencing the Debtor\'s pre-petition indebtedness and Existing Equity Interests shall be deemed cancelled, discharged, and of no further force or effect, including without limitation: (a) the First Lien Credit Agreement; (b) the Second Lien Credit Agreement; (c) the 8.25% Senior Notes Indenture, dated as of November 1, 2020, between the Debtor and Fidelitas Trust Company, as Indenture Trustee; (d) all certificates representing shares of common stock of the Debtor; and (e) all other agreements and instruments related thereto. **Section 8.01 --- Distribution Record Date**

The Distribution Record Date shall be the close of business on the date that is five (5) Business Days after the Confirmation Date (approximately January 24, 2025). Only holders of record of Allowed Claims and Interests as of the Distribution Record Date shall be entitled to receive distributions under this Plan on account of such Claims and Interests.

**Section 8.02 --- Timing of Distributions**

Distributions under this Plan shall commence on the Effective Date or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter, except as otherwise specifically provided herein. Distributions on account of Claims that become Allowed after the Effective Date shall be made within thirty (30) days after such Claims become Allowed.

**Section 8.03 --- Distribution Agent**

Reorganized Oakvale shall act as Distribution Agent, or may designate a third-party distribution agent to effectuate distributions under this Plan. Reorganized Oakvale shall be responsible for all costs and expenses of the Distribution Agent.

**Section 8.04 --- Fractional Shares and De Minimis Distributions**

No fractional shares of New Common Stock shall be issued under this Plan. Fractional share entitlements shall be rounded down to the nearest whole share. No Cash payment shall be made on account of any fractional share entitlement. No distribution of Cash or other property having a value of less than \$50.00 shall be made to any holder of an Allowed Claim. Any such amount shall be retained by Reorganized Oakvale.

**Section 8.05 --- Undeliverable Distributions**

If any distribution to a holder of an Allowed Claim is returned as undeliverable, no further distribution shall be made to such holder unless and until the Distribution Agent is notified of such holder\'s then-current address. All undeliverable distributions shall be held by the Distribution Agent for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days after the Effective Date. After such 180-day period, all unclaimed property shall be forfeited and deemed unclaimed, and the holder\'s entitlement to such distribution shall be discharged and forever barred, and the undeliverable distributions shall be returned to Reorganized Oakvale.

**Section 8.06 --- Withholding and Reporting**

Reorganized Oakvale and the Distribution Agent shall be authorized to deduct and withhold from any distribution under this Plan such amounts as may be required to be withheld under the Internal Revenue Code or any applicable state, local, or foreign tax law. Such withheld amounts shall be deemed to have been distributed to and received by the applicable holder for all purposes of this Plan. Reorganized Oakvale shall comply with all applicable tax reporting obligations in connection with the Plan transactions, including without limitation the preparation and filing of IRS Form 8937 (Report of Organizational Actions Affecting Basis of Securities) within forty-five (45) days of the Effective Date.

**Section 8.07 --- Setoffs**

Reorganized Oakvale may, but shall not be required to, set off against any Claim and the distributions to be made pursuant to this Plan on account of such Claim any and all claims, rights, and Causes of Action that the Debtor or Reorganized Oakvale may have against the holder of such Claim, to the extent such setoff is permitted under applicable law. Neither the failure to set off any such claim nor the allowance of any Claim under this Plan shall constitute a waiver or release by the Debtor or Reorganized Oakvale of any such claim, right, or Cause of Action.

**Section 13.08 --- Tax Matters**

The Debtor anticipates that the transactions contemplated by this Plan, including the exchange of Claims for New Common Stock, will qualify for the stock-for-debt exception to cancellation-of-debt income under Section 108(e)(8) of the Internal Revenue Code, thereby reducing the amount of cancellation-of-debt (\"COD\") income recognized by the Debtor. Notwithstanding the application of such exception, the Debtor estimates that approximately \$98,700,000 in COD income will be recognized and must be offset by attribute reduction under Section 108(b) of the Internal Revenue Code, including reduction of the Debtor\'s net operating loss carryforwards.

The Debtor intends to make a Section 382(l)(5) election in its next filed federal income tax return, if eligible, to avoid the application of an annual Section 382 limitation on the use of pre-change net operating losses. If the Debtor is not eligible for or does not make a Section 382(l)(5) election, Section 382(l)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code shall apply, and the Debtor\'s annual use of pre-change net operating losses will be limited based on the value of the Reorganized Debtor immediately after the ownership change. The Tax Opinion from Merriweather & Cain, CPA, a condition precedent to the Effective Date as set forth in Section 9.01(k), shall analyze the applicability of Sections 382(l)(5) and 382(l)(6) to the Plan transactions. The Debtor acknowledges that the Section 382 analysis depends in part on the final determination of the Reorganized Debtor\'s shareholder composition, including the identification and ownership percentages of individual creditors receiving New Common Stock, which cannot be fully determined until the equity distributions are allocated on or after the Distribution Record Date.

Reorganized Oakvale shall prepare and file IRS Form 8937 (Report of Organizational Actions Affecting Basis of Securities) within forty-five (45) days of the Effective Date.

**B. Voting Results and Classification**

9\. The Plan designates the following classes of Claims and Interests. The Court finds that the classification of Claims and Interests under the Plan complies with Sections 1122 and 1123(a)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code, as each class contains only Claims or Interests that are substantially similar to the other Claims or Interests within such class:

> **(a) Class 1 --- First Lien Claims. Class 1 consists of the First Lien Claims in the aggregate allowed amount of \$415,000,000. Class 1 is Impaired under the Plan. The holders of Class 1 Claims voted to accept the Plan by the requisite majorities: 97.3% in amount and 88.2% in number of the holders casting ballots in Class 1 voted to accept the Plan. The treatment of Class 1 under the Plan provides for each holder of an Allowed First Lien Claim to receive, on a pro rata basis: (i) its pro rata share of new first-lien exit term loans under the Exit Term Loan Credit Agreement in the aggregate principal amount of \$250,000,000; and (ii) its pro rata share of 72% of the reorganized common equity of Reorganized Oakvale, consisting of 7,200,000 shares of the 10,000,000 authorized and issued shares of common stock (the \"Reorganized Common Stock\").**
>
> **(b) Class 2 --- Second Lien Claims.** Class 2 consists of the Second Lien Claims in the aggregate allowed amount of \$105,000,000. Class 2 is Impaired under the Plan. The holders of Class 2 Claims voted to accept the Plan by the requisite majorities: 91.6% in amount and 78.9% in number of the holders casting ballots in Class 2 voted to accept the Plan. The treatment of Class 2 under the Plan provides for each holder of an Allowed Second Lien Claim to receive, on a pro rata basis: (i) its pro rata share of 18% of the Reorganized Common Stock, consisting of 1,800,000 shares; and (ii) its pro rata share of Series A Warrants to purchase up to 500,000 additional shares of Reorganized Common Stock at a strike price of \$12.50 per share, exercisable for a period of five years from the Effective Date.
>
> **(c) Class 3 --- Senior Unsecured Notes Claims.** Class 3 consists of the Claims arising under the 8.25% Senior Notes due 2027 in the aggregate allowed amount of \$92,000,000, for which Fidelitas Trust Company serves as indenture trustee. Class 3 is Impaired under the Plan. For distribution purposes, the holders of Class 3 Claims are included with Class 5 (General Unsecured Claims) and shall receive the same treatment on a pari passu basis. The holders of Class 3 Claims voted separately and accepted the Plan by the requisite majorities: 84.1% in amount and 67.4% in number of the holders casting ballots in Class 3 voted to accept the Plan.
>
> **(d) Class 4 --- Other Priority Claims.** Class 4 consists of Other Priority Claims entitled to priority under Section 507(a) of the Bankruptcy Code (other than Administrative Claims and Priority Tax Claims). Class 4 is Unimpaired under the Plan. The holders of Class 4 Claims are deemed to have accepted the Plan pursuant to Section 1126(f) of the Bankruptcy Code and were not entitled to vote on the Plan. Each holder of an Allowed Class 4 Claim shall receive payment in full in cash on the Effective Date or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter.
>
> **(e) Class 5 --- General Unsecured Claims.** Class 5 consists of General Unsecured Claims in the estimated aggregate allowed amount of approximately \$47,000,000 in trade claims plus the Class 3 Senior Unsecured Notes Claims (\$92,000,000) that share in the Class 5 distribution on a pari passu basis. Class 5 is Impaired under the Plan. The holders of Class 5 Claims voted to accept the Plan by the requisite majorities: 76.8% in amount and 62.3% in number of the holders casting ballots in Class 5 voted to accept the Plan. The treatment of Class 5 under the Plan provides for each holder of an Allowed General Unsecured Claim (including Class 3 claimants) to receive, on a pro rata basis: (i) its pro rata share of 10% of the Reorganized Common Stock, consisting of 1,000,000 shares; and (ii) its pro rata share of beneficial interests in the Litigation Trust.
>
> **(f) Class 6 --- Existing Equity Interests.** Class 6 consists of all Existing Equity Interests in the Debtor, including all issued and outstanding shares of common stock, preferred stock, options, warrants, and other rights to acquire equity interests. Class 6 is Impaired under the Plan. The holders of Existing Equity Interests are deemed to have rejected the Plan pursuant to Section 1126(g) of the Bankruptcy Code because they will receive no distribution and no property under the Plan, and all Existing Equity Interests will be cancelled, extinguished, and discharged on the Effective Date.

10\. The Court finds that the total equity reconciliation under the Plan is as follows: Class 1 (7,200,000 shares) + Class 2 (1,800,000 shares) + Class 5 (1,000,000 shares) = 10,000,000 shares, representing 100% of the authorized and issued Reorganized Common Stock. In addition, the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation will authorize 2,000,000 shares of preferred stock, which will remain undesignated and unissued as of the Effective Date.

11\. Each Impaired class that was entitled to vote on the Plan (Classes 1, 2, 3, and 5) has accepted the Plan by the requisite majorities under Section 1126(c) of the Bankruptcy Code --- that is, at least two-thirds in amount and more than one-half in number of the holders of Claims in each such class that actually voted. Class 6, as noted, is deemed to have rejected the Plan pursuant to Section 1126(g), and the Plan is confirmable with respect to Class 6 pursuant to Section 1129(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, as set forth below.

**D. Compliance with Section 1129(b) --- Cramdown**

14\. Because Class 6 (Existing Equity Interests) is deemed to have rejected the Plan pursuant to Section 1126(g) of the Bankruptcy Code, the Debtor has requested that the Court confirm the Plan pursuant to the \"cramdown\" provisions of Section 1129(b) of the Bankruptcy Code with respect to Class 6.

15\. The Court finds that the Plan does not discriminate unfairly with respect to Class 6. Class 6 holders receive no distribution under the Plan, and no class of Claims or Interests that is junior to or equal in priority with Class 6 receives any distribution or retains any property under the Plan on account of such junior or equal Claims or Interests.

16\. The Court further finds that the Plan is fair and equitable with respect to Class 6. Because the holders of Claims in classes senior to Class 6 --- specifically, Classes 1, 2, 3, and 5 --- are not being paid in full, the absolute priority rule requires that holders of Existing Equity Interests in Class 6 receive no distribution under the Plan. The Plan satisfies this requirement: all Existing Equity Interests will be cancelled, extinguished, and discharged on the Effective Date, and holders of Existing Equity Interests will receive no distribution or property under the Plan.

17\. Accordingly, the requirements of Section 1129(b)(1) and (b)(2)(C) of the Bankruptcy Code are satisfied, and the Plan is confirmable notwithstanding the deemed rejection by Class 6.

73\. This Confirmation Order is a final, appealable order within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 158(a).

75\. As set forth in Section IV above and in Article IX, Section 9.01(a) of the Plan, the Effective Date is conditioned upon this Confirmation Order becoming a \"Final Order\" as defined in the Plan. A \"Final Order,\" as so defined, requires that the time to appeal, petition for certiorari, or move for reargument, reconsideration, or rehearing has expired and that no such appeal, petition, or motion is pending. Pursuant to Article IX, Section 9.02 of the Plan, the condition that this Confirmation Order shall have become a Final Order may not be waived.

76\. The Court finds that there is no just reason for delay and that this Confirmation Order should take effect immediately upon entry. However, the Effective Date of the Plan is separately and independently conditioned on this Order becoming a Final Order, which requires the expiration of the appeal period under Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 8002(a)(1) without the filing of any notice of appeal (or, if an appeal is filed, the resolution of such appeal in favor of confirmation). Accordingly, the Effective Date of the Plan shall not occur until such time as the Confirmation Order has become a Final Order.

77\. The Court notes that any party in interest may file a notice of appeal from this Confirmation Order within the fourteen (14)-day appeal period. Any party in interest considering whether to file an appeal should be mindful of the Outside Date of April 17, 2025, and the consequences of the Effective Date not occurring by such date.

**[I. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT]{.underline}**

Oakvale Industrial Holdings, Inc. (the \"Debtor\"), as debtor and debtor in possession in the above-captioned chapter 11 case, by and through its undersigned counsel, Thornfield & Associates LLP, hereby files this Status Report (this \"Status Report\") regarding the current status of the conditions precedent to the Effective Date of the Debtor\'s Second Amended Plan of Reorganization (Dkt. No. 487) (as confirmed, and as may be modified, supplemented, or amended from time to time, the \"Plan\"), which was confirmed by order of this Court entered on January 17, 2025 (Dkt. No. 512) (the \"Confirmation Order\"). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Plan or the Confirmation Order, as applicable.

Pursuant to Article IX, Section 9.01 of the Plan, the Effective Date is defined as the first Business Day after all conditions precedent set forth in Section 9.01 of the Plan have been satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 9.02 of the Plan. The Debtor is targeting an Effective Date of **February 18, 2025**. The Plan provides that if all conditions precedent to the Effective Date have not been satisfied or waived on or before the date that is ninety (90) days after entry of the Confirmation Order (the \"Outside Date\"), the Confirmation Order shall be vacated, the Plan shall be null and void in all respects, and the rights of all parties in interest shall be restored to the status quo ante as though the Confirmation Order had never been entered. The Outside Date under the Plan is **April 17, 2025**.

The purpose of this Status Report is to inform the Court and all parties in interest of the status of each condition precedent to the Effective Date identified in Article IX, Section 9.01 of the Plan and to identify remaining open items. The Confirmation Hearing on the Plan was held on January 13, 14, and 15, 2025, and the Court entered the Confirmation Order on January 17, 2025. The Debtor submits this Status Report in the ordinary course to facilitate transparency and to apprise the Court and stakeholders of the Debtor\'s progress toward emergence from chapter 11.

**[II. BACKGROUND]{.underline}**

The Debtor commenced its chapter 11 case by filing a voluntary petition for relief under chapter 11 of title 11 of the United States Code (the \"Bankruptcy Code\") on March 14, 2024 (the \"Petition Date\"). Since the Petition Date, the Debtor has continued to operate its business and manage its property as debtor in possession pursuant to Sections 1107(a) and 1108 of the Bankruptcy Code. The Office of the United States Trustee for the District of Delaware appointed the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the \"Committee\") on April 2, 2024.

The Court established July 15, 2024 as the general bar date for filing proofs of claim against the Debtor (the \"General Bar Date\") and September 10, 2024 as the bar date for governmental units (the \"Governmental Bar Date\"). The Debtor\'s Disclosure Statement in support of the Plan was approved by order of the Court on October 30, 2024 (Dkt. No. 389). The deadline for casting ballots on the Plan (the \"Voting Deadline\") was December 20, 2024. All impaired classes of claims entitled to vote on the Plan --- specifically, Class 1 (First Lien Secured Claims), Class 2 (Second Lien Secured Claims), Class 3 (Senior Unsecured Notes Claims), Class 4 (General Unsecured Claims), and Class 5 (Convenience Claims) --- accepted the Plan by the requisite majorities in number and amount. Class 6 (Existing Equity Interests) is deemed to reject the Plan and is not entitled to any distribution thereunder.

The Confirmation Hearing was held on January 13, 14, and 15, 2025, and the Court entered the Confirmation Order on January 17, 2025. The fourteen-day appeal period under Rule 8002(a) of the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure expired on January 31, 2025.

As of the Petition Date, the Debtor\'s capital structure consisted of the following funded debt obligations: (a) \$415,000,000 in aggregate principal amount of first lien term loan obligations (the \"First Lien Debt\"), for which Greystone National Bank, N.A. serves as administrative agent; (b) \$105,000,000 in aggregate principal amount of second lien term loan obligations (the \"Second Lien Debt\"), for which Capstone Credit Partners, LLC serves as administrative agent; and (c) \$92,000,000 in aggregate principal amount of 9.50% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2026 (the \"Senior Unsecured Notes\"), for which Fidelitas Trust Company serves as indenture trustee. In addition, the Debtor scheduled approximately \$47,000,000 in trade claims and other general unsecured obligations.

Under the Plan, distributions to the Debtor\'s creditors are structured as follows: First Lien lenders will receive \$250,000,000 in exit term loans plus 72% of the reorganized equity of Reorganized Oakvale (7,200,000 shares of New Common Stock). Second Lien lenders will receive 18% of the reorganized equity (1,800,000 shares of New Common Stock) plus Series A Warrants for 500,000 shares of New Common Stock at an exercise price of \$12.50 per share. General Unsecured Creditors (including holders of Senior Unsecured Notes Claims and General Unsecured Claims in Classes 3 and 4) will receive in the aggregate 10% of the reorganized equity (1,000,000 shares of New Common Stock) plus beneficial interests in the Litigation Trust. The total authorized and issued reorganized equity on the Effective Date will be 10,000,000 shares of New Common Stock.

Administrative claims are estimated at approximately \$38,200,000 in the aggregate, consisting of approximately \$23,500,000 in professional fee claims, approximately \$6,700,000 in claims arising under Section 503(b)(9) of the Bankruptcy Code, and approximately \$8,000,000 in other administrative expense claims. Priority Tax Claims are estimated at approximately \$4,600,000.

**[Section 2.2 --- Exit ABL Revolver Commitment]{.underline}**

Greystone National Bank, N.A. (\"Greystone\" or the \"ABL Arranger\") hereby commits to arrange, and to act as sole lead bookrunner and administrative agent for, a senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility (the \"Exit ABL Revolver\" and, together with the Exit Term Loan, the \"Exit Facilities\") in an aggregate commitment amount of \$75,000,000 (with availability subject to a borrowing base) on the terms and conditions set forth herein and in Exhibit B attached hereto.

The Exit ABL Revolver shall be made available to the Reorganized Borrower on the Closing Date and shall be guaranteed by the same Guarantors as the Exit Term Loan. Greystone National Bank, N.A. shall serve as Administrative Agent for the Exit ABL Revolver.

The Exit ABL Revolver shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to Term SOFR (with a floor of 0.00%) plus 200 basis points, subject to a pricing grid based on average excess availability, and shall mature on the fourth anniversary of the Closing Date. The borrowing base shall consist of 85% of eligible accounts receivable plus 65% of eligible inventory, less customary reserves as determined by the ABL Agent.

The proceeds of the Exit ABL Revolver shall be used for working capital and general corporate purposes of the Reorganized Borrower and its subsidiaries, including funding of the Professional Fee Escrow (up to \$26,000,000) and other Effective Date payments as needed.

The Exit ABL Revolver shall be secured by a first priority lien on ABL Priority Collateral (accounts receivable, inventory, deposit accounts, and related assets) and a second priority lien on Term Loan Priority Collateral, in each case subject to the terms of an intercreditor agreement between the Term Loan Agent and the ABL Agent (the \"Intercreditor Agreement\"). The Intercreditor Agreement is an essential component of the Exit Facility documentation and must be executed simultaneously with the definitive credit agreements for the Exit Facilities. No funding shall be made under the Exit ABL Revolver in the absence of an executed Intercreditor Agreement.

**[Section 2.3 --- Several (Not Joint) Obligations]{.underline}**

The commitments of each Commitment Party hereunder are several and not joint. Ledgerstone\'s commitment is limited solely to the Exit Term Loan, and Greystone\'s commitment is limited solely to the Exit ABL Revolver. Neither Commitment Party shall have any liability for the performance or non-performance of the other Commitment Party\'s obligations hereunder. No Commitment Party shall be required to fund any amount in excess of its respective commitment as set forth in this Section 2.

**[Section 4 --- \"SunGard\" Provisions / Certain Funds]{.underline}**

The parties acknowledge and agree that the conditions set forth in Section 3 of this Commitment Letter are the only conditions to the Commitment Parties\' obligations to fund the Exit Facilities on the Closing Date. The Commitment Parties acknowledge that the conditions precedent are based on the limited-conditionality framework commonly referred to as the \"SunGard\" construct, and the definitive credit agreements shall not contain representations, warranties, covenants, events of default, or other conditions to borrowing that are not customary for exit financing facilities of this type or size or that would effectively create additional conditions to the initial funding of the Exit Facilities beyond those expressly set forth in Section 3 of this Commitment Letter.

For the avoidance of doubt, the definitive credit agreements may contain customary representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default that are consistent with the terms described in Exhibits A and B attached hereto; provided that the accuracy of representations and warranties (other than the \"SunGard\" representations identified in Exhibit A) shall not be a condition to the initial funding of the Exit Facilities on the Closing Date unless otherwise expressly set forth in Section 3.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Commitment Parties reserve the right to exercise the Flex Provisions set forth in Section 5, and the exercise of any such Flex Provisions shall not constitute a breach of the limited-conditionality construct described in this Section 4.

The limited-conditionality construct set forth in this Section 4 applies exclusively to the initial funding of the Exit Facilities on the Closing Date. Subsequent borrowings and the issuance of letters of credit under the Exit ABL Revolver after the Closing Date shall be subject to customary conditions precedent, including the accuracy of representations and warranties in all material respects and the absence of any Default or Event of Default.

**[Section 5 --- Flex Provisions]{.underline}**

The Commitment Parties shall have the right, in their sole discretion, to modify certain terms of the Exit Facilities (the \"Flex Provisions\") if Ledgerstone or Greystone, as applicable, determines in good faith that such modifications are advisable to ensure successful syndication of the applicable Exit Facility.

**Pricing Flex (Exit Term Loan).** Ledgerstone may increase the interest rate margin on the Exit Term Loan by up to 75 basis points (from Term SOFR + 475 bps to Term SOFR + 550 bps) and/or increase the SOFR floor by up to 25 basis points (from 0.75% to 1.00%). In addition, Ledgerstone may require an original issue discount (\"OID\") of up to 2.00% of the aggregate principal amount (i.e., an issue price of 98.0).

**Pricing Flex (Exit ABL Revolver).** Greystone may increase the interest rate margin on the Exit ABL Revolver by up to 50 basis points (from Term SOFR + 200 bps to Term SOFR + 250 bps) and/or modify the applicable pricing grid by corresponding amounts.

**Structural Flex.** The Commitment Parties may modify amortization schedules, mandatory prepayment provisions (including excess cash flow sweep percentages and step-down thresholds), financial covenant levels, and negative covenant baskets, in each case to the extent consistent with market terms for comparable exit financing facilities for borrowers of similar size and credit profile.

Any exercise of Flex Provisions shall be communicated to the Borrower in writing no later than ten (10) Business Days prior to the anticipated Closing Date, and shall set forth with reasonable specificity the modifications being made and the rationale therefor (to the extent such rationale can be provided without disclosing confidential syndication information).

The exercise of any Flex Provisions in accordance with this Section 5 shall not be deemed a failure of any condition precedent set forth in Section 3 or a termination event under Section 10, and the Borrower shall cooperate with the Commitment Parties in implementing any such modifications in the Exit Facility Documentation.

**RIDGEMONT INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.,** a Delaware corporation, EIN 27-4831956,

**ORDER APPROVING DEBTOR\'S MOTION FOR AUTHORIZATION TO IMPLEMENT KEY EMPLOYEE RETENTION PLAN PURSUANT TO 11 U.S.C. §§ 363(b) AND 503(c)**

Dated: June 28, 2024

This matter coming before the Court upon the Motion of Oakvale Industrial Holdings, Inc. (the \"Debtor\") for Entry of an Order Authorizing the Debtor to Implement a Key Employee Retention Plan (the \"KERP Motion\"), filed on June 10, 2024 (Dkt. No. 187). The Debtor commenced this Chapter 11 case by filing a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of Title 11 of the United States Code (the \"Bankruptcy Code\") on March 14, 2024 (the \"Petition Date\"). The Debtor continues to operate its business and manage its properties as debtor-in-possession pursuant to Sections 1107(a) and 1108 of the Bankruptcy Code. No trustee or examiner has been appointed in this case.

The Debtor is a leading manufacturer and supplier of specialty valves, actuators, and flow-control systems for the petrochemical and water-treatment industries, with its principal place of business located at 4500 Commerce Parkway, Suite 200, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, the Debtor reported revenues of approximately \$385 million. As of the Petition Date, the Debtor\'s total funded indebtedness was approximately \$612 million, consisting of first lien and second lien term loan facilities, and the Debtor\'s outstanding trade payables totaled approximately \$47 million. The Debtor also holds Department of Defense supplier qualification MIL-V-24509, and the retention of qualified technical personnel is critical to maintaining this qualification and preserving the Debtor\'s eligibility for government contracts.

The Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the \"Committee\") was appointed by the United States Trustee on April 2, 2024. The Committee was given due and proper notice of the KERP Motion and, after arms\'-length negotiations with the Debtor, does not object to the relief sought in the KERP Motion as modified by the agreed-upon revisions reflected herein, including the reduction in certain individual allocations and the addition of forfeiture provisions. The Office of the United States Trustee (the \"U.S. Trustee\") was given notice of the KERP Motion and filed a limited response (Dkt. No. 214), the substance of which was addressed and resolved on the record at the hearing.

The Debtor is represented by Thornfield & Associates LLP (Rebecca S. Thornfield, Partner, and Marcus D. Wynn, Senior Associate) as restructuring counsel in this Chapter 11 case. The Debtor retained Petworth Advisory Group as its financial advisor, and Samantha K. Rourke, Managing Director of Petworth Advisory Group, provided a declaration in support of the KERP Motion (Dkt. No. 188) (the \"Rourke Declaration\"), demonstrating through a market analysis of comparable retention programs in Chapter 11 cases involving similarly situated manufacturing debtors that the proposed KERP is reasonable in scope, amount, and structure, and that the retention of the identified key employees is necessary to preserve the going-concern value of the Debtor\'s estate and to consummate a successful plan of reorganization.

The Court having considered the KERP Motion, the Rourke Declaration, the Committee\'s statement of non-objection (Dkt. No. 226), the U.S. Trustee\'s limited response (Dkt. No. 214), the evidence presented, and the arguments of counsel at the hearing held on June 27, 2024, and finding that due and adequate notice of the KERP Motion was given under the circumstances, and that good cause exists for the relief granted herein, the Court hereby makes the following findings of fact and conclusions of law:

**[FINDINGS OF FACT]{.underline}**

The Court makes the following findings of fact, each of which is supported by the record in this case:

1\. The Debtor, with the assistance of Petworth Advisory Group, has identified fourteen (14) key employees (each, a \"KERP Participant\" and, collectively, the \"KERP Participants\") who are critical to the Debtor\'s ongoing operations and to the successful reorganization of the Debtor\'s business and affairs. The specific KERP Participants, their titles, and their respective KERP allocations are set forth in the Participant Schedule attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and incorporated herein by reference.

2\. Petworth Advisory Group conducted a comprehensive market analysis of retention programs approved in Chapter 11 cases involving manufacturing companies of comparable size, complexity, and industry profile. The Rourke Declaration details the methodology and results of this analysis, which the Court finds credible and persuasive.

3\. The aggregate cost of the KERP is \$2,150,000 (Two Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars), which represents approximately 0.56% of the Debtor\'s FY2023 revenue of \$385 million and is within the range of comparable retention programs approved in similar Chapter 11 cases.

4\. The KERP Participants include the Debtor\'s Chief Executive Officer, Gerald T. Harwick, and Chief Financial Officer, Dana M. Pellegrino, along with twelve (12) other employees holding positions at the vice president, director, and senior manager level. These individuals possess specialized knowledge regarding the Debtor\'s manufacturing processes, proprietary engineering designs, customer relationships, DOD supplier qualification (MIL-V-24509), supply chain operations, government contract compliance, and financial reporting functions that cannot be readily replaced.

5\. The loss of any of these employees would materially and adversely affect the Debtor\'s ability to maintain ongoing operations, preserve the going-concern value of the estate, retain DOD supplier qualification, and consummate a successful plan of reorganization. The Rourke Declaration establishes that replacement costs for comparable manufacturing and engineering personnel in the Debtor\'s geographic markets would substantially exceed the proposed KERP allocations.

6\. The KERP does not constitute a prohibited \"pay to stay\" bonus under Section 503(c)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code. With respect to Gerald T. Harwick (CEO) and Dana M. Pellegrino (CFO), who are \"insiders\" as defined in Section 101(31) of the Bankruptcy Code, the Debtor has demonstrated through competent evidence that each individual has received a bona fide offer of employment from another business at the time the KERP Motion was filed and that the proposed retention payments are essential to the retention of these individuals. With respect to all other KERP Participants, the payments are not transfers or obligations to or for the benefit of insiders and are justified under the business judgment standard of Section 503(c)(3).

7\. The Committee, after good-faith negotiations with the Debtor, secured certain modifications to the originally proposed KERP, including (a) a reduction in certain individual allocations from the amounts initially proposed, and (b) the addition of a forfeiture provision requiring that each KERP Participant remain continuously employed by the Debtor through and including the Effective Date of the Debtor\'s plan of reorganization in order to receive his or her KERP payment. These modifications, which are reflected in this Order, are reasonable and appropriate.

8\. The KERP is a reasonable exercise of the Debtor\'s business judgment and is in the best interests of the Debtor\'s estate and its creditors.

**[CONCLUSIONS OF LAW]{.underline}**

Based upon the foregoing findings of fact, the Court reaches the following conclusions of law:

1\. This Court has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 157 and 1334 and the Amended Standing Order of Reference from the United States District Court for the District of Delaware, dated February 29, 2012. Venue is proper in this District pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1408 and 1409.

2\. This matter is a core proceeding within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2), and this Court may enter a final order consistent with Article III of the United States Constitution.

3\. The Debtor has satisfied the legal standards applicable to the approval of the KERP under Section 503(c) of the Bankruptcy Code. With respect to Gerald T. Harwick (CEO) and Dana M. Pellegrino (CFO), who are \"insiders\" within the meaning of Section 101(31) of the Bankruptcy Code, the Debtor has met the heightened requirements of Section 503(c)(1), including demonstrating that (a) each individual has a bona fide job offer from another business at the time of the filing of the KERP Motion, (b) the services provided by each individual are essential to the survival of the Debtor\'s business, and (c) the amount of each retention payment does not exceed ten times the amount of the mean retention bonus given to nonmanagement employees during the calendar year in which the payment is to be made, and in any event is not greater than twenty-five percent of the amount of any similar bonus given to the individual for any prior fiscal year. With respect to all other KERP Participants, the KERP satisfies the business judgment standard of Section 503(c)(3) because the payments are not transfers or obligations to or for the benefit of insiders and are justified by the facts and circumstances of this case, as demonstrated by the record.

4\. The Debtor has provided adequate and sufficient notice of the KERP Motion to all required parties in interest, including the Committee, the Office of the United States Trustee, Greystone National Bank, N.A. (as Administrative Agent under the First Lien Credit Agreement), Capstone Credit Partners, LLC (as Administrative Agent under the Second Lien Credit Agreement), and all other parties entitled to notice under the Bankruptcy Rules and this Court\'s orders. No further or additional notice is required.

5\. Good cause exists for the entry of this Order and the relief granted herein.

**[ORDER]{.underline}**

Based upon the foregoing findings of fact and conclusions of law, **IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, ADJUDGED, AND DECREED THAT:**

**1. KERP Approved.** The KERP Motion is **GRANTED**. The Debtor is authorized, but not directed, to implement the Key Employee Retention Plan (the \"KERP\") in accordance with the terms set forth herein and in the Participant Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**2. Aggregate Amount.** The aggregate maximum amount payable under the KERP shall not exceed **\$2,150,000** (Two Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars). Individual allocations among the fourteen (14) KERP Participants are as set forth in Exhibit A hereto.

**3. Payment Trigger.** KERP payments shall become due and payable upon the occurrence of the Effective Date of the Debtor\'s plan of reorganization (as such term is defined in any plan of reorganization confirmed in this Chapter 11 case) (the \"Effective Date\"). Payment of each KERP Participant\'s KERP allocation shall be made on the Effective Date or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter, but in no event later than ten (10) business days following the Effective Date.

**4. Continued Employment Requirement; Forfeiture. Each KERP Participant must remain continuously employed by the Debtor (or any successor entity, including without limitation Reorganized Oakvale Industrial Holdings, Inc. or any acquiring entity in a sale transaction) through and including the Effective Date to be eligible to receive his or her KERP payment. If a KERP Participant\'s employment terminates for any reason --- whether by voluntary resignation, termination for cause, or termination without cause --- prior to the Effective Date, such KERP Participant shall forfeit his or her entire KERP allocation, and such forfeited amount shall automatically revert to the Debtor\'s estate. The forfeiture shall be automatic and self-executing and shall require no further order of this Court.**

> *Exception:* Notwithstanding the foregoing, if a KERP Participant\'s employment is terminated by the Debtor without cause within thirty (30) calendar days prior to the Effective Date, such KERP Participant shall remain eligible for fifty percent (50%) of his or her KERP allocation, payable on the same terms and conditions as all other KERP payments under this Order. For the avoidance of doubt, this exception shall not apply to any KERP Participant who voluntarily resigns or whose employment is terminated for cause during the thirty-day period prior to the Effective Date.

**5. No Acceleration.** KERP payments shall not be accelerated under any circumstances, including, without limitation, upon the conversion of this Chapter 11 case to a case under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code, the dismissal of this case, or the appointment of a Chapter 11 trustee. In the event of any such conversion, dismissal, or appointment, all obligations under the KERP shall terminate immediately and no amounts shall be payable to any KERP Participant.

**6. Administrative Expense Priority.** KERP payments authorized and payable under this Order shall constitute allowed administrative expense claims under Section 503(b)(1)(A) of the Bankruptcy Code and shall be entitled to priority of payment under Section 507(a)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code.

**7. Tax Withholding.** The Debtor is authorized and directed to withhold and remit all applicable federal, state, and local income taxes, employment taxes, and other employment-related withholdings from KERP payments in accordance with applicable law.

**8. No Modification Without Court Approval.** The Debtor shall not modify, amend, supplement, or otherwise alter the KERP, or increase any individual KERP allocation, without further order of this Court entered after notice and a hearing in accordance with Sections 102(1) and 503(c) of the Bankruptcy Code.

**9. Reporting.** The Debtor shall include information regarding the status of the KERP and KERP payments in its monthly operating reports filed with the Court and the U.S. Trustee. Without limitation, if any KERP Participant\'s employment terminates prior to the Effective Date for any reason, the Debtor shall disclose such termination and the resulting forfeiture of the applicable KERP allocation in its next monthly operating report following such termination.

**10. Reservation of Rights.** Nothing in this Order shall prejudice the rights of any party in interest to object to the allowance of any administrative expense claim arising under or related to the KERP on grounds other than the authorization granted herein, including, without limitation, the right to assert that the conditions for payment set forth in this Order have not been satisfied.

**11. Retention of Jurisdiction.** This Court retains exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine all matters arising from, related to, or connected with the implementation, interpretation, and enforcement of this Order, including any disputes regarding the forfeiture provisions set forth in Paragraph 4 above.

The Litigation Trust is established for the sole purpose of liquidating and distributing the Litigation Trust Assets for the benefit of the Beneficiaries in an expeditious but orderly manner, with no objective to continue or engage in the conduct of a trade or business, except to the extent reasonably necessary to, and consistent with, the liquidating purpose of the Litigation Trust as contemplated by this Agreement and the Plan. The Parties intend that the Beneficiaries shall be treated as the grantors and deemed owners of the Litigation Trust for federal income tax purposes. **Section 2.02 --- Purpose of the Litigation Trust**

> \(a\) to hold, manage, administer, prosecute, compromise, settle, collect, and enforce the Assigned Causes of Action for the benefit of the Beneficiaries;

> \(b\) to distribute Net Litigation Proceeds to the Beneficiaries, after payment or reservation for Litigation Trust expenses, in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Plan;

> \(d\) to comply with all applicable tax, reporting, and regulatory requirements; and
>
> \(e\) to wind up the affairs of the Litigation Trust and dissolve as expeditiously as is consistent with maximizing recoveries for the Beneficiaries.

The Litigation Trust shall not engage in any trade or business and shall not hold or acquire any assets other than the Litigation Trust Assets and any Permitted Investments. **Section 3.02 --- Powers and Duties of the Litigation Trustee**

Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Plan, and the Confirmation Order, the Litigation Trustee shall have full power and authority to take any and all actions that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the accomplishment of the purposes of the Litigation Trust, including without limitation the following:

> \(a\) **Prosecution and Resolution of Claims.** The Litigation Trustee shall have the exclusive right, power, and authority to prosecute, litigate, compromise, settle, or abandon any and all Assigned Causes of Action in the name of the Litigation Trust, in such manner and on such terms as the Litigation Trustee deems to be in the best interests of the Beneficiaries, subject to the settlement approval requirements set forth in Section 5.03 hereof.
>
> \(b\) **Retention of Professionals.** The Litigation Trustee may retain, engage, and compensate attorneys, accountants, investigators, financial advisors, consultants, and other professionals as reasonably necessary to carry out the purposes of the Litigation Trust and the duties of the Litigation Trustee, subject to the budget and oversight provisions of Section 3.06 and the Trust Advisory Board approval requirements set forth in Section 4.02. The Litigation Trustee may engage such professionals on such terms as the Litigation Trustee deems appropriate, including hourly, fixed-fee, contingency, or hybrid fee arrangements.
>
> \(c\) **Settlements.** The Litigation Trustee shall have authority to enter into settlements of the Assigned Causes of Action in accordance with Section 5.03 hereof, including settlements valued at less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) individually without prior Trust Advisory Board approval.
>
> \(d\) **Investment of Trust Funds.** The Litigation Trustee may invest Litigation Trust Assets held in cash in Permitted Investments as described in Section 3.05 hereof.
>
> \(e\) **Distributions.** The Litigation Trustee shall make distributions of Net Litigation Proceeds to the Beneficiaries in accordance with Article VII hereof.
>
> \(f\) **Execution of Documents.** The Litigation Trustee may execute and deliver all documents, instruments, and agreements on behalf of the Litigation Trust as may be necessary or appropriate in connection with the administration and operation of the Litigation Trust.
>
> \(g\) **Tax Compliance.** The Litigation Trustee shall file or cause to be filed all required federal, state, and local tax returns and information returns and shall comply with all applicable tax reporting obligations.
>
> \(h\) **General Authority.** The Litigation Trustee may take all other actions that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the foregoing and that are consistent with the purpose of the Litigation Trust as described in Section 2.02 hereof.

The Litigation Trustee shall act in a fiduciary capacity for the benefit of the Beneficiaries in all matters relating to the administration and operation of the Litigation Trust. The Litigation Trustee shall exercise the powers granted hereunder in good faith and in accordance with the standard of care set forth in Section 3.03 hereof.

**Section 3.03 --- Standard of Care; Limitation of Liability**

The Litigation Trustee shall discharge the duties and exercise the powers set forth in this Agreement in good faith, with the care, skill, and diligence of a reasonably prudent person in a like position under similar circumstances, and in a manner that the Litigation Trustee reasonably believes to be in the best interests of the Beneficiaries. In discharging such duties, the Litigation Trustee shall be entitled to rely upon information, opinions, reports, and statements prepared or presented by professionals retained by the Litigation Trustee, provided that such reliance is in good faith and the Litigation Trustee has no reason to believe that such information, opinions, reports, or statements are materially inaccurate or misleading.

The Litigation Trustee shall not be personally liable for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith and in the reasonable belief that such

action or inaction was in the best interests of the Beneficiaries and was within the scope of authority conferred upon the Litigation Trustee by this Agreement, the Plan, and the Confirmation Order. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Litigation Trustee shall be personally liable for losses or damages to the Litigation Trust or the Beneficiaries caused by the Litigation Trustee\'s willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud, as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.

No Beneficiary shall have any claim against the Litigation Trustee, any member of the Trust Advisory Board, or any professional retained by the Litigation Trustee for any increase or decrease in the value of the Litigation Trust Assets, except as expressly provided herein with respect to willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud.

**Section 3.04 --- Compensation of the Litigation Trustee**

The Litigation Trustee shall receive compensation for services rendered in connection with the Litigation Trust at the rate of Six Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$650.00) per hour for time actually spent on Litigation Trust matters. The Litigation Trustee\'s total compensation for any given twelve-month period shall not exceed Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$350,000) per annum (the \"Annual Compensation Cap\"), unless the Trust Advisory Board approves an increase in such cap for good cause shown. Any such increase shall be documented in writing and, if material, reported to the Beneficiaries in the next quarterly report.

In addition to hourly compensation, the Litigation Trustee shall be entitled to reimbursement of all reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of the Litigation Trustee\'s duties hereunder, including without limitation travel expenses, communication charges, copying and printing costs, postage, and similar charges. The Litigation Trustee shall not incur any individual expense in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000) without prior approval of the Trust Advisory Board, except for routine expenses in the ordinary course of administration.

Compensation and reimbursable expenses shall be paid from the Litigation Trust Assets on a quarterly basis, upon the Litigation Trustee\'s submission of detailed written invoices to the Trust Advisory Board reflecting the time spent, services rendered, and expenses incurred during the applicable quarter. The Trust Advisory Board shall review and approve such invoices within fifteen (15) days of receipt. In the event of any dispute regarding compensation or expenses, the matter shall be submitted to the Bankruptcy Court for resolution.

**Success Fee.** In addition to the hourly compensation and expense reimbursement described above, the Litigation Trustee shall be entitled to a success fee (the \"Success Fee\") equal to three percent (3%) of Net Litigation Proceeds in excess of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) in the aggregate recovered by the Litigation Trust during the term of the Litigation Trust. The Success Fee shall be calculated and paid at the time of each distribution to Beneficiaries, and shall be payable from the Litigation Trust Assets prior to distribution to the Beneficiaries. The Success Fee is intended to align the interests of the Litigation Trustee with those of the Beneficiaries by incentivizing the maximization of recoveries.

**Section 3.05 --- Investment of Trust Funds**

Litigation Trust Assets held in the form of cash shall be invested solely in the following categories of investments (collectively, \"Permitted Investments\"):

> \(a\) direct obligations of, or obligations the principal of and interest on which are unconditionally guaranteed by, the United States of America, in each case maturing within one (1) year from the date of investment;
>
> \(b\) money market funds that are rated AAAm (or the equivalent) by at least one nationally recognized statistical rating organization, as defined in Section 3(a)(62) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934;
>
> \(c\) demand and time deposits, certificates of deposit, or bankers\' acceptances at financial institutions that are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (\"FDIC\"), provided that amounts on deposit shall not exceed applicable FDIC insurance limits at any single institution unless collateralized by U.S. government obligations; or
>
> \(d\) such other short-term, liquid, low-risk investments as may be approved in advance by the Trust Advisory Board in writing.

The Litigation Trustee shall not make any speculative, illiquid, or high-risk investments. All investment activity shall be consistent with the Litigation Trust\'s status and purpose as a liquidating trust, and the Litigation Trustee shall at all times maintain sufficient liquidity to fund anticipated litigation costs and administrative expenses.

**Section 3.06 --- Budget and Reporting**

Within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, the Litigation Trustee shall prepare and submit to the Trust Advisory Board for its review and approval an initial annual budget for the Litigation Trust (the \"Initial Budget\"). The Initial Budget shall include the Litigation Trustee\'s good faith estimates of: (a) legal fees and litigation costs for the prosecution of each category of Assigned Causes of Action; (b) the Litigation Trustee\'s anticipated compensation and expenses; (c) administrative costs, including accounting, tax preparation, insurance, and related expenses; and (d) reserves for distributions to Beneficiaries and for disputed claims. Subsequent annual budgets shall be submitted for Trust Advisory Board approval at least thirty (30) days before the beginning of each fiscal year of the Litigation Trust.

The Litigation Trustee shall provide quarterly written reports (each, a \"Quarterly Report\") to the Trust Advisory Board and to the Beneficiaries (or to a representative of the Beneficiaries designated for such purpose, if applicable), which Quarterly Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) a summary of the status of each Assigned Cause of Action, including any material developments during the quarter; (b) a statement of receipts, disbursements, and cash balances during and at the end of the quarter; (c) the Litigation Trustee\'s estimated timeline for resolution of the Assigned Causes of Action; and (d) any other information that the Litigation Trustee or the Trust Advisory Board deems material to the interests of the Beneficiaries. Quarterly Reports shall be provided within forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar quarter.

In addition, the Litigation Trustee shall file an annual accounting with the Bankruptcy Court, on or before April 30 of each year for the preceding calendar year, setting forth the financial position and activities of the Litigation Trust for the applicable period. Such annual accounting shall be served on the United States Trustee and on counsel for the Reorganized Debtor.

**[ARTICLE IV --- TRUST ADVISORY BOARD]{.underline}**

**Section 4.01 --- Composition**

The Trust Advisory Board shall consist of three (3) members. The initial members of the Trust Advisory Board shall be designated by the Committee prior to the Effective Date, and their identities shall be set forth on Schedule B hereto. The Committee shall designate the initial Trust Advisory Board members no later than \[●\] Business Days prior to the Effective Date.

In the event that the Committee has been dissolved as of the Effective Date (as may occur upon the Effective Date or upon substantial consummation of the Plan in accordance with Section 1102(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code), the initial Trust Advisory Board members shall be those individuals identified on Schedule B hereto. \[Schedule B to be completed prior to execution of this Agreement.\]

Members of the Trust Advisory Board shall serve in their capacity as fiduciaries of the Beneficiaries and shall exercise their duties in good faith and with the care of a reasonably prudent person in a like position. Members of the Trust Advisory Board shall serve without compensation, but shall be entitled to reimbursement of reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of their duties from the Litigation Trust Assets, subject to the approval of the Litigation Trustee.

**Section 4.02 --- Powers of the Trust Advisory Board**

The Trust Advisory Board shall have the following powers and responsibilities:

> \(a\) to approve or disapprove settlements of Assigned Causes of Action with a value of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) or more individually or One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) or more in the aggregate, as required by Section 5.03 hereof;
>
> \(b\) to review and approve the annual budget of the Litigation Trust, including the Initial Budget, as provided in Section 3.06 hereof;
>
> \(c\) to approve the retention and compensation of professionals retained by the Litigation Trustee in cases where the anticipated compensation to any single professional exceeds One Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$100,000) per year;
>
> \(d\) to approve any increase to the Litigation Trustee\'s Annual Compensation Cap as provided in Section 3.04 hereof;
>
> \(e\) to approve investments of Litigation Trust cash assets in investments other than those expressly described in clauses (a) through (c) of Section 3.05 hereof;
>
> \(f\) to consult with and advise the Litigation Trustee on matters of strategy, timing, and administration of the Litigation Trust; and
>
> \(g\) to exercise such other powers as are expressly granted to the Trust Advisory Board under this Agreement.

The Trust Advisory Board shall act in an advisory and oversight capacity only and shall not have direct authority to prosecute, litigate, settle, or abandon any Assigned Cause of Action or to bind the Litigation Trust in any manner. Such authority rests exclusively with the Litigation Trustee, subject to the approval and oversight requirements set forth in this Agreement.

**Section 4.03 --- Meetings; Quorum; Actions**

The Trust Advisory Board shall meet at least quarterly, or more frequently as may be called by the Litigation Trustee or by any two (2) members of the Trust Advisory Board, upon not less than five (5) Business Days\' prior written notice to all members and to the Litigation Trustee (unless such notice is waived). A quorum of the Trust Advisory Board shall consist of two (2) of three (3) members. Actions of the Trust Advisory Board shall be taken by majority vote of the members present (in person, by telephone, or by videoconference) at a meeting at which a quorum is present. Meetings of the Trust Advisory Board may be held in person, by telephone, or by videoconference, at the discretion of the members. Actions may also be taken by unanimous written consent of all members without a meeting, and such consent may be delivered by electronic transmission.

**Section 4.04 --- Vacancies; Removal; Resignation**

A vacancy on the Trust Advisory Board, whether resulting from death, resignation, removal, or incapacity, shall be filled by the affirmative vote of the remaining member or members of the Trust Advisory Board. In the event that no members of the Trust Advisory Board remain, the Bankruptcy Court shall appoint successor members upon application by the Litigation Trustee or any Beneficiary. Any successor member shall meet the same standards of independence and absence of conflict as apply to initial members.

A member of the Trust Advisory Board may be removed for cause by order of the Bankruptcy Court, upon motion of the Litigation Trustee, any other member of the Trust Advisory Board, or any Beneficiary. For purposes of this Section, \"cause\" includes willful misconduct, gross negligence, fraud, conviction of a felony, or persistent failure to attend meetings or perform duties.

A member of the Trust Advisory Board may resign upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the Litigation Trustee and the other members of the Trust Advisory Board. A resignation shall become effective upon the earlier of the appointment of a successor or the expiration of such thirty (30) day notice period.

**Section 5.02 --- Prosecution of Assigned Causes of Action**

The Litigation Trustee shall have sole and exclusive discretion in determining the strategy, timing, manner, and conduct of prosecution of the Assigned Causes of Action. The Litigation Trustee\'s decisions regarding whether and how to prosecute any Assigned Cause of Action shall be made in the exercise of the Litigation Trustee\'s reasonable business judgment and fiduciary duties to the Beneficiaries and shall not be subject to review or challenge except as otherwise provided in this Agreement.

The Litigation Trustee may retain one or more law firms, attorneys, or other professionals as litigation counsel in connection with the prosecution of the Assigned Causes of Action, on such terms and conditions (including hourly, fixed-fee, contingency, or hybrid fee arrangements) as the Litigation Trustee deems appropriate and in the best interests of the Beneficiaries. The retention of any professional whose anticipated annual compensation exceeds One Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$100,000) shall be subject to the prior approval of the Trust Advisory Board, as provided in Section 4.02(c) hereof.

The Litigation Trustee may, in the exercise of reasonable business judgment, determine to abandon any Assigned Cause of Action that the Litigation Trustee concludes has insufficient value to justify the costs and resources of continued prosecution, provided that the Litigation Trustee shall give written notice to the Trust Advisory Board at least fifteen (15) days prior to the effective date of any such abandonment. The Trust Advisory Board may, within such fifteen (15) day period, object to the proposed abandonment, in which case the matter shall be submitted to the Bankruptcy Court for determination.

**Section 5.03 --- Settlement Authority**

The Litigation Trustee\'s authority with respect to the settlement, compromise, or other consensual resolution of any Assigned Cause of Action shall be as follows:

> \(a\) **Settlements Under \$500,000.** The Litigation Trustee shall have sole authority, without the consent or approval of the Trust Advisory Board or the Bankruptcy Court, to settle or compromise any Assigned Cause of Action where the total settlement value is less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) individually.
>
> \(b\) **Settlements of \$500,000 or More.** The settlement or compromise of any Assigned Cause of Action where the total settlement value is Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) or more individually, or where the aggregate value of settlements entered into during any twelve-month period equals or exceeds One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000), shall require the prior written approval of the Trust Advisory Board.
>
> \(c\) **Settlements Exceeding \$2,000,000.** The settlement or compromise of any Assigned Cause of Action where the total settlement value exceeds Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) shall require, in addition to Trust Advisory Board approval, the approval of the Bankruptcy Court after notice and a hearing in accordance with the Bankruptcy Rules and any applicable local rules of the Bankruptcy Court.

All settlements shall be on terms that the Litigation Trustee reasonably believes are in the best interests of the Beneficiaries, taking into account the merits of the claim, the risks and costs of continued litigation, the likelihood and timing of recovery, and such other factors as the Litigation Trustee deems relevant.

**[ARTICLE VI --- SUCCESSOR TRUSTEES; VACANCY]{.underline}**

**Section 6.01 --- Resignation of Litigation Trustee**

The Litigation Trustee may resign upon sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to the Trust Advisory Board and the Bankruptcy Court. The notice of resignation shall state the effective date of the resignation, which shall not be earlier than the sixtieth (60th) day after delivery of such notice. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no resignation of the Litigation Trustee shall become effective until a successor Litigation Trustee has been duly appointed and has accepted such appointment in accordance with Section 6.03 hereof. The resigning Litigation Trustee shall continue to serve and perform duties hereunder until such successor is in place.

**Section 6.02 --- Removal of Litigation Trustee**

The Litigation Trustee may be removed for cause by order of the Bankruptcy Court, upon motion of the Trust Advisory Board, the Reorganized Debtor, or any Beneficiary holding Litigation Trust Interests representing in excess of five percent (5%) of the aggregate Litigation Trust Interests then outstanding. For purposes of this Section, \"cause\" shall mean: (a) willful misconduct in the performance of duties under this Agreement; (b) gross negligence in the performance of duties under this Agreement; (c) fraud, dishonesty, or criminal conduct; (d) conviction of, or plea of guilty or *nolo contendere* to, a felony; or (e) a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice thereof to the Litigation Trustee. The Bankruptcy Court shall determine whether cause exists for removal after notice and a hearing.

**Section 6.03 --- Appointment of Successor**

Upon a vacancy in the position of Litigation Trustee (whether by reason of resignation, removal, death, incapacity, or otherwise), the Trust Advisory Board shall, within thirty (30) days of such vacancy, designate and appoint a successor Litigation Trustee. If the Trust Advisory Board fails to designate a successor within such thirty (30) day period, the Bankruptcy Court shall appoint a successor Litigation Trustee upon motion of any interested party, including any Beneficiary or the Reorganized Debtor.

Any successor Litigation Trustee must be a natural person who: (a) is independent and does not have a material conflict of interest with respect to the Assigned Causes of Action or the Beneficiaries; (b) has not been convicted of a felony; and (c) possesses the qualifications, experience, and ability necessary to discharge the duties of Litigation Trustee under this Agreement.

Upon the appointment and acceptance by a successor Litigation Trustee, the predecessor Litigation Trustee (or, in the event of the predecessor\'s death or incapacity, the predecessor\'s personal representative or estate) shall promptly transfer and deliver to the successor all Litigation Trust Assets, books, records, files, documents, correspondence, and other materials in the predecessor\'s possession or control relating to the Litigation Trust, and shall execute such instruments and take such other actions as the successor may reasonably request to effectuate the transfer.

**[ARTICLE VII --- DISTRIBUTIONS TO BENEFICIARIES]{.underline}**

**Section 7.01 --- Distribution Procedures**

The Litigation Trustee shall make distributions of Net Litigation Proceeds to the Beneficiaries at least annually, or more frequently in the Litigation Trustee\'s discretion, as and when the Litigation Trustee determines that funds are available for distribution after taking into account the need for reserves for estimated future expenses, litigation costs, contingencies, and disputed claims. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no distribution shall be required at any time if the aggregate amount available for distribution is less than One Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$100,000).

Distributions shall be made pro rata based on each Beneficiary\'s Litigation Trust Interest (i.e., in proportion to the ratio that each Beneficiary\'s Allowed General Unsecured Claim bears to the aggregate amount of all Allowed General Unsecured Claims in Class 5). The Litigation Trustee shall maintain a distribution register reflecting each Beneficiary\'s Litigation Trust Interest and the cumulative distributions made to each Beneficiary.

Prior to making any distribution, the Litigation Trustee shall maintain a reasonable reserve for: (a) estimated future litigation costs and expenses; (b) the Litigation Trustee\'s anticipated compensation and expense reimbursements; (c) administrative and overhead costs of the Litigation Trust; (d) the Disputed Claims Reserve described in Section 7.02; and (e) any other contingencies that the Litigation Trustee, in the exercise of reasonable business judgment, deems appropriate.

Distributions shall be made by check or wire transfer of immediately available funds to the address or account information on file with the Litigation Trustee for each Beneficiary. It shall be the responsibility of each Beneficiary to provide the Litigation Trustee with current and accurate address and payment information. The Litigation Trustee shall not be liable for any distribution that is delayed, misdirected, or lost as a result of a Beneficiary\'s failure to provide current and accurate information.

**Section 7.02 --- Disputed Claims Reserve**

To the extent that any General Unsecured Claim in Class 5 remains disputed, contingent, or unliquidated as of any distribution date, the Litigation Trustee shall reserve a pro rata portion of available distributions attributable to such disputed claim (the \"Disputed Claims Reserve\") pending the resolution of such disputed claim by the Bankruptcy Court or by agreement of the parties. The amount of the Disputed Claims Reserve attributable to any particular disputed claim shall be based on the lesser of (a) the asserted amount of such claim and (b) such amount as the Bankruptcy Court may estimate for reserve purposes under Section 502(c) of the Bankruptcy Code.

Upon the allowance of a disputed claim, the Litigation Trustee shall distribute to the holder of such newly Allowed Claim its pro rata share of the Disputed Claims Reserve (net of any distributions previously made to other Beneficiaries on account of such amount). Upon the disallowance of a disputed claim, the amount reserved for such disallowed claim shall be redistributed to the Beneficiaries on the next distribution date.

**Section 7.03 --- Unclaimed Distributions**

Any distribution that remains unclaimed for a period of ninety (90) days after the date on which such distribution was mailed or otherwise transmitted to a Beneficiary shall be deemed an unclaimed distribution. Unclaimed distributions shall be redistributed to the remaining Beneficiaries on a pro rata basis on the next succeeding distribution date, and the Beneficiary who failed to claim such distribution shall have no further claim thereto.

The Litigation Trustee shall make reasonable efforts to locate Beneficiaries, including by conducting address searches and sending reminder notices prior to deeming any distribution unclaimed. The costs of such efforts shall be borne by the Litigation Trust as an administrative expense.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- TAX PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.01 --- Tax Treatment of the Litigation Trust**

The Litigation Trust is intended to be treated for federal income tax purposes as a \"grantor trust\" within the meaning of Sections 671 through 679 of the IRC, with the Beneficiaries treated as the grantors and deemed owners of the Litigation Trust. All Parties shall report consistently with the foregoing characterization on all applicable federal, state, and local tax returns and information reports.

The Beneficiaries shall be treated as receiving their respective shares of the Litigation Trust Assets on the Effective Date for federal income tax purposes, and shall thereafter be required to report their allocable shares of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit of the Litigation Trust on their individual (or entity-level) tax returns, in accordance with their Litigation Trust Interests.

The Litigation Trust shall obtain a separate taxpayer identification number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service, which shall be used for all tax reporting and withholding purposes of the Litigation Trust. The Litigation Trustee shall take all actions necessary to preserve the Litigation Trust\'s status as a grantor trust and shall not take any action that would jeopardize such status.

**Section 8.02 --- Tax Reporting**

The Litigation Trustee shall file, or cause to be filed, all required federal, state, and local tax returns and information returns with respect to the Litigation Trust, including without limitation IRS Form 1041 (or any successor form) and any other applicable returns. The Litig

ation Trustee shall file such returns on a timely basis, including extensions.

The Litigation Trustee shall provide each Beneficiary with an annual statement, no later than April 15 of each year for the preceding calendar year (or such later date as may be permitted by applicable law), reflecting such Beneficiary\'s allocable share of Litigation Trust income, deductions, credits, and other items required to be reported for federal income tax purposes. Such statements shall be provided on IRS Form 1099 (or such other form as may be appropriate or required by the Internal Revenue Service).

The Debtor\'s existing tax advisors, Merriweather & Cain, CPA, located at 200 Penn Street, Suite 1400, Philadelphia, PA 19106, may be retained by the Litigation Trustee for tax compliance and reporting purposes on behalf of the Litigation Trust, subject to the Litigation Trustee\'s right, in the exercise of discretion, to engage alternative tax counsel, accountants, or advisors as the Litigation Trustee deems appropriate.

**Section 8.03 --- Tax Withholding**

The Litigation Trustee shall withhold and pay over to the applicable taxing authority all amounts required to be withheld under applicable federal, state, or local tax laws in connection with distributions or allocations made to or for the benefit of the Beneficiaries. Any amounts so withheld shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as distributions to the applicable Beneficiary and shall reduce the amount of cash or other property otherwise distributable to such Beneficiary.

The Litigation Trustee may require each Beneficiary to provide a properly completed IRS Form W-9 (or, for non-U.S. Beneficiaries, the applicable IRS Form W-8) prior to making any distribution. The Litigation Trustee may withhold any distribution pending receipt of such form.

**[ARTICLE IX --- INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE]{.underline}**

The Litigation Trust shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Litigation Trustee, and the Litigation Trustee\'s agents, employees, and representatives, from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, suits, proceedings, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including without limitation reasonable attorneys\' fees and disbursements) arising out of or related to the Litigation Trustee\'s performance of, or failure to perform, duties under this Agreement, the Plan, or the Confirmation Order, except to the extent that such claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses are finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to have been caused by the Litigation Trustee\'s willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud.

**Section 9.02 --- Indemnification of Trust Advisory Board**

The Litigation Trust shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each member of the Trust Advisory Board from and against any and all claims, demands, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to such member\'s service on the Trust Advisory Board, except to the extent that such claims, losses, or damages are finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to have been caused by such member\'s willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud. The indemnification obligations set forth in this Section 9.02 shall be payable from the Litigation Trust Assets and shall survive the dissolution of the Litigation Trust and the resignation or removal of the applicable member.

**Section 9.03 --- Insurance**

The Litigation Trustee may obtain, at the expense of the Litigation Trust, errors and omissions insurance, professional liability insurance, or other coverage as the Litigation Trustee deems appropriate to protect the Litigation Trust, the Litigation Trustee, and the members of the Trust Advisory Board in connection with the performance of their respective duties, subject to the prior approval of the Trust Advisory Board as to the premium amount and terms of such coverage.
